name: Angarakha & Ghagra Choli
info: Traditional Rajasthani attire featuring the Angarakha for men and vibrant Ghagra Choli for women.
history: Evolved in the harsh desert climates, these garments use bright colors to contrast with the arid landscape.
trivia: The Angarakha means 'body protector' and features a unique asymmetrical tie on the chest.
funFact: Rajasthani women's Ghagras often feature heavy mirror work that sparkles beautifully in the desert sun!

name: Dhotar Kurta & Nauvari Saree
info: Classic Maharashtrian wear. Men wear the white Dhotar Kurta, while women drape the 9-yard Nauvari saree.
history: The Nauvari drape originated from Maratha women warriors who needed to ride horses while fighting.
trivia: Unlike a regular saree, the Nauvari is worn like a dhoti, tucked at the back, eliminating the need for a petticoat.
funFact: During the Peshwa era, women would fight alongside men on the battlefield wearing the very same Nauvari drape!

name: Punjabi Kurta & Saree
info: The quintessential Bengali look featuring a Dhoti and Punjabi (Kurta) for men, and elegant Sarees for women.
history: Handloom weaving of cotton and silk sarees has been a significant part of Bengal's history for centuries.
trivia: The men's upper garment is uniquely referred to as a 'Punjabi' in Bengal, not just a 'Kurta'.
funFact: The traditional red-and-white 'Lal-Paar' saree is iconic to Bengal and is considered highly auspicious for festivals.

name: Gamosa
info: A white rectangular piece of hand-woven cotton cloth with a red border and woven motifs.
history: It holds deep cultural significance in Assam, used as a towel, a wrapper, or offered to guests as a sign of respect.
trivia: The word 'Gamosa' literally translates to 'something to wipe the body with'.
funFact: During the Bihu festival, a beautifully woven Gamosa called 'Bihuwan' is gifted to elders as a token of love and respect.

name: Kediyu & Chaniya Choli
info: Vibrant and heavily embroidered festive wear from Gujarat, prominently worn during Garba.
history: Rooted in the pastoral communities of Gujarat, the garments evolved with intricate mirror work and embroidery.
trivia: The Kediyu is a frilled, gathered top worn by men that uniquely flares out when they spin during dances.
funFact: The sheer weight of a traditional Chaniya Choli's embroidery can easily surpass 5-7 kilograms!

name: Kurta Pajama & Salwar Kameez
info: The comfortable and colorful daily and festive wear of Punjab, featuring loose trousers and tunics.
history: The Salwar Kameez was brought to the Indian subcontinent by Muslim invaders and was widely adopted in the Punjab region.
trivia: The traditional Punjabi Salwar features beautiful heavy pleating, known as the 'Patiala Salwar'.
funFact: The Patiala Salwar was originally designed for the Maharaja of Patiala, but became wildly popular among women!

name: Mundu & Mundum Neriyathum
info: The elegant, minimalist white and gold attire of Kerala. The Mundu is worn by men, and the two-piece Mundum Neriyathum by women.
history: The two-piece drape is one of the oldest forms of the Indian saree, surviving in Kerala for centuries.
trivia: The pure white color reflects the tropical heat, while the 'Kasavu' (gold border) indicates festive importance.
funFact: Traditionally, the gold border on the Mundu was woven with actual pure gold threads by the royal weavers!

name: Panche & Lungi
info: Traditional lower garments worn in Karnataka. The Panche is a white wrap, while the Lungi is a casual, colorful tube skirt.
history: These wraps are perfectly suited for the humid climate of South India and have been worn since antiquity.
trivia: The Panche is typically worn during religious ceremonies and formal occasions, while the Lungi is casual home wear.
funFact: In many traditional South Indian households, there's a strict rule: you cannot enter the puja (prayer) room wearing a stitched garment!

name: Pheran
info: A long, loose winter cloak worn by both men and women in Kashmir.
history: Believed to trace back to Central Asian cloaks or introduced by the Mughals to help locals survive the harsh winters.
trivia: A traditional Pheran is wide enough to let the wearer carry a 'Kangri' (fire pot) underneath it for warmth.
funFact: Despite modern heating, the Pheran remains the most popular winter garment in Kashmir purely due to its Kangri-holding capability!

name: Veshti & Kanchipuram Saree
info: Men wear the white Veshti, while women adorn the world-famous, rich silk Kanchipuram sarees.
history: Kanchipuram weavers claim descent from Sage Markanda, the master weaver of gods who wove tissue from lotus fiber.
trivia: A genuine Kanchipuram saree's border and body are woven separately and then joined with a specialized interlocking stitch.
funFact: The silk used in a Kanchipuram saree is so strong that the fabric can easily last for multiple generations!
